subject: Request: exception path for third-party cache + runtime data scope
messages:

Cc: 
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: HealthCorp DPA redline - caching subprocessor ask

Marcus / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal completed a pass on the DPA and flagged the runtime caching/third-party cache clause — specifically the potential use of FastCache as a transient KV cache for inference state. Our security team requires written confirmation that: (1) FastCache will only hold encrypted KV artifacts, (2) TTLs are bounded to 24 hours or less, and (3) there is an audit trail for access.

We'd like to propose an exception path that would allow FastCache in non-production environments for pilot traffic, and a scoped production carveout if the above controls are implemented and reviewed. Please see attached HC-DPA-redline-v3.docx with suggested language next to section 4.2.

Can you coordinate with Product/Security at Redwood and provide a one-page mitigation summary plus an updated redline? Timetable: we need an answer for procurement by end of this week to stay on the Q3 onboarding timeline.

Best,
Nora Klein
Sr. Counsel, HealthCorp

Subject: Re: HealthCorp DPA redline - caching subprocessor ask

Nora — thanks for the clear ask and the redline. Looping in Olga (Security) and Kimberly (Product) to coordinate so we can get you the mitigation summary and a proposed carveout language. A couple of quick context notes from Product: Redwood uses short-lived encrypted KV caches for specific runtime performance optimizations (prefix cache + KV for decoder state). In most cases these caches are internal, but for the HealthCorp pilot we evaluated FastCache as a managed option to reduce latency spikes in the EU region during early traffic.

Open questions we need to confirm:
- Does HealthCorp consider presence of encrypted KV cache (no model weights, no unencrypted user PII) to be within the DPA runtime scope?
- Are the 24h TTL and audit log requirements hard constraints or negotiable (we can offer 6–12h for production, pilot at 24h)?

We aim to produce: (A) a 1-page mitigation summary (encryption keys, KMS integration, access controls, RBAC, audit hooks), (B) a suggested DPA carveout paragraph that limits cache to non-personally-identifiable inference metadata + TTL and (C) the FastCache vendor security pack (attached).

Will target a draft back by EOW.

—Marcus

Team — reviewing Nora's redline and Marcus' notes. Security position + required checklist below. Nora, leaving you on the loop for transparency.

Minimum technical controls we need to attest to for any caching subprocessor exception:
- Encryption at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS1.3); customer-specific KMS integration required for prod carveout (customer keys stored in their KMS).
- Per-tenant keying or envelope encryption: caching layer must not share encryption keys across HealthCorp tenants/environments.
- TTL capped at 12 hours for production; pilot can be 24 hours with explicit approval and additional monitoring.
- No retention of raw request payloads that contain identifiable customer data. We will only store derived inference metadata (token ids, cached prefix vectors) and will strip content classified as PII by our classifier.
- Full audit logs (access, key ops, vendor admin ops) retained for 180 days and accessible to HealthCorp via secure log forwarding or SFTP.
- Quarterly pen-test from FastCache with report to Redwood and HealthCorp for the duration of the carveout.

Product tradeoffs to call out (Jordan / Kimberly): enabling FastCache for HealthCorp reduces tail latency by ~30% on long-sequence jobs but introduces an external subprocessor and additional operational steps (KMS onboarding, key rotation cadence, additional billing meter). If procurement requires the 24h TTL in production we should provide mitigations such as strict sampling and encryption of sensitive prefixes plus an SLA carveout to control exposure.

Action items:
- Kimberly: prepare a single-paragraph DPA carveout and a short runbook for KMS onboarding (who works with customer infra).
- Jordan: confirm telemetry hooks and log-forward format; can we provide a sample log export?
- Marcus: please confirm whether HealthCorp will accept 12h TTL for production; if not we'll escalate the business tradeoff.

I'll draft the mitigation summary and include the technical controls above — should be ready in the next 6 hours.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Security Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: HealthCorp DPA redline - caching subprocessor ask

Nora / HealthCorp team — thanks for the patience. Attached is a proposed single-paragraph carveout and the one-page mitigation summary Olga compiled. Summary of key points:

- Scope: exception limited to transient KV cache used for runtime inference acceleration. The cache will not store model weights or raw request text; only encrypted inference state and derived metadata.
- Controls: AES-256 at rest, TLS1.3 in transit, customer KMS option for production, 12-hour TTL in production (pilot permitted at 24 hours), audit logs available via secure forward, quarterly vendor pen-tests.
- Operational: KMS onboarding runbook attached; Redwood SRE will own key rotation schedule and can white-glove the initial integration with HealthCorp infra.

If HealthCorp legal accepts the paragraph below we will sign the redline and execute the DocuSign flow. If HealthCorp insists on 24h TTL in production we need to align on compensating controls (sampling, no-PII policy enforced by classifier, extended logging) — this will require an SLA amendment and further procurement negotiation.

Proposed paragraph (for insertion into section 4.2):
"Notwithstanding other provisions of this Agreement, the Parties agree that Redwood may engage a third-party caching subprocessor (\"Cache Subprocessor\") for the sole purpose of transient runtime KV caching to optimize inference latency. Cache Subprocessor use is limited to encrypted inference state and derived metadata; no raw request content or model weights shall be stored. Cache TTL in production must not exceed twelve (12) hours unless separately agreed in writing. Redwood will provide audit logs and evidence of vendor security attestations on request. Customer-specific KMS integration is available for production deployments upon execution of the carveout.
"
Next steps: Nora — could you confirm whether your legal team can accept this language? If accepted we will prepare an updated redline and DocuSign packet today.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Management, Redwood Inference
